Commentary.Commentary: The morning freshness will be there in the surface and the Indian bowlers will like to gain advantage from that with the new ball. The Australian bowlers have done their job and now it's time for their batsmen to step up and deliver. They will be out soon to commence their innings. Stay tuned.

Right then, it took the Aussies just one ball to pick the last Indian wicket. An excellent performance by their bowlers. They were right on the button from the very first ball on Day 1. Their speedsters destroyed India's top order and it required a patient century by Cheteshwar Pujara to provide some respectability to their total. His stands with the lower half were crucial and credit should be given to them for hanging in there.

OUT! Strangled down the leg side! Hazlewood bowls a gentle loosener, it's short and going down the leg side. Shami tries to play the pull shot but ends up gloving it behind. Paine dives full length to his left and takes a fine catch. They appeal and the finger has gone up. India are all out for 250!
It's time to get underway. The Australian players are entering the arena. Mohammed Shami and Jasprit Bumrah are the Indian batsmen. Josh Hazlewood to complete his over.

Pitch report - Brendon Julian is by the pitch side and mentions that there is some more coarse grass on the surface than Day 1. He feels that the Indian bowlers will have to get their lengths right. Informs that only 19 from the 250 runs scored yesterday came down the ground which tells the two-paced nature of the wicket. He believes that today will be the best day to bat but the batsmen will have to watch out for the new-ball spell.

Cheteshwar Pujara was a satisfied man last evening and has already called it one of his top five knocks. Also, he feels that India have posted a decent total on the board as he found the pitch to be two-paced and not easy for stroke-making. Let's wait and watch how Australia will respond with the bat. First up, they will have to pick India's last wicket.

The first day of this Test series lived up to the expectations as we witnessed plenty of action. There was some extraordinary pace bowling, quite a few loose shots, turn and bounce for the spinner and a knock of heroic patience. We're greedy, we want more and we're back for some more dose of quality Test cricket. Hello and welcome everyone, stay with us for further updates.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

It's time to sign off. We witnessed 87.5 overs of quality Test cricket and are expecting more of the same on Day 2. India also have the powerhouse in their bowling to succeed and Australia's weakest suit will be put under pressure. Promises to be a riveting contest between bat and ball. Do join us at 1030 local (0000 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

For India, it looks like a sorry scorecard. The top order got blown away in no time and they were reeling at 41/4 at one stage. After that, Cheteshwar Pujara found an ally in Rohit Sharma and together they formed a partnership. Just when it seemed that Sharma will run away with the show, a moment of brain fade resulted in his demise from the crease. Pujara though didn't lose hope and kept on adding partnerships with the lower order. Courtesy his hundred, the visitors have got a respectable total on the board now although it still appears below par on this surface.

End of an outstanding day of Test cricket. It all started with the Aussie speedsters derailing the Indian innings in the morning. Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins were stupendous with their efforts as they brought the visiting team on the mat. All of them picked up a couple of wickets apiece and Nathan Lyon also contributed to the cause by hunting down the dangerous looking Rohit Sharma and Rishabh Pant.

OUT! Pujara is well short! Take a bow, Pat Cummins. They needed something magical to dismiss Pujara and it has come through an inspirational piece of fielding by Pat. A fuller length ball on middle, Pujara gently pushes it towards mid on and wants to retain strike for the next over. Hence he takes a chance and calls his partner through. However, Cummins attacks the ball, throws himself up in the air, has just one stump to aim at and he scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end. All that happened in one motion. Wow. It's an incredible effort from someone who has bowled 19 overs in the day under hot conditions. What an athlete! The umpire goes upstairs to check for the run out and Pujara is not even in the frame. End of an outstanding knock and he walks back to a good ovation from the crowd. That also will be Stumps on Day 1.
Appeal for a run out! Pat Cummins has scored a direct hit at the non-striker's end. Pujara appears to be short. Let's find out.
Boom! Another firm shot. A length delivery outside off, Pujara goes hard at it and drills it through mid off for a couple of runs. 250 up for India!

Pujara is putting on a show. He has fought hard to reach this stage and with nothing much to lose, he is playing his shots freely. A short delivery around off, Che leans back and ramps it over the slip cordon. The third man fielder cuts it off and they take a couple of runs.
Straighter in line, Pujara clips it through mid-wicket and comes back for the second run.
In the air, safe! Short in length and outside off, Shami stands tall and plays it over point for a run.
Short again, just around off, Pujara tries to force it through the line but misses.
SIX! Bang! What a knock this is turning out to be! Starc digs in a short delivery outside off, Pujara exercises his arms and slams it over backward point for a biggie. Vital runs.

FOUR! Finds the gap with perfection. A length ball on middle and leg, Pujara uses his wrists and flicks it beautifully behind square leg. He pierces the gap between fine leg and square leg with precision.
Fuller in length and on middle, Pujara takes a calculative risk and chips it over mid on. The mid-wicket fielder pulls it back and they take two.
A rising delivery on off, Pujara goes on his toes and plays it down through point. A run is turned down.
A length delivery angling away from the batsman, Pujara drives it on the up but fails to beat the cover fielder.
A back foot defense off the last delivery to end the over.
Play and a miss! Short delivery, bowled at a good pace, Shami is early into the pull shot and hence takes a blow on his body.
Good length ball on off, Shami stays back footed and plays it to covers.
Shortish and on middle, Pujara swivels and pulls it down to fine leg. Strangely, takes a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes on the back foot to a shortish ball and blocks it safely.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it but misses.
Hurries up the batsman with a sharp shorter one. Pujara gloves his pull shot towards square leg and takes a run.
Short and angling away from the batsman, Pujara rocks back and cuts it through point for a couple of runs.

Here it is, 16th Test ton for Cheteshwar Pujara, third against Australia and first Down Under! A big moment for him and what a knock he has played in a crisis. Wickets were tumbling around him but he never lost hope and has dragged India's total close to 250 now. Reaches the milestone with a gentle nudge in front of square leg for a couple. The crowd applauds the effort from the Indian number 3.
Once again there is room on offer outside off and Shami runs it down to third man for a run. Pujara returns on strike!
Width on offer outside off, Shami flashes and misses.
FOUR! Pujara moves to 99 now! A much-better pull shot, this. Another short delivery by Josh and he hooks it behind square leg for a boundary.

SIX! Pujara breaks into the 90s! Not in a convincing manner but he won't care much at this stage. Takes on the challenge to pull the short delivery but it takes the top edge and flies over fine leg for a maximum. 5000 Test runs for him as well.

Appeal for a caught behind, not given! Hazlewood alters his length to go short and bowls it outside off. Pujara tries to play the square cut but fails to middle his shot. There is certainly some noise as it goes behind to Paine. He appeals but nothing from the umpire. No DRS taken.
Fuller and around off, Pujara tries to go hard at it but his bat turns in his hands and he gets it away off the inside edge through square leg.
Good length delivery in the line of the stumps, Pujara turns it in the gap on the leg side but denies the single. He now needs to change gears and pacers are bowling from both ends.
Serves it on a driving length outside off, Pujara makes a leave. He is 11 short of his hundred.
A length ball on off, Shami defends it from the crease to the off side.
FOUR! Starc eyes a yorker but ends up slipping a low full toss outside off, Shami reaches out for it and squeezes it through point for a boundary.
Mohammed Shami is the new batsman.

OUT! Bowled 'em! It was only a matter of time. Starc was trying to do this on the previous ball as well but the line wasn't good. But this time, he is right on the money. Full and sharp and straight, Ishant is beaten for pace as he is late in bringing his bat down. It goes right through his defense, brushes his pads and then cannons onto the stumps. Starc gets his second wicket and gives a stare to Sharma. Ishant doesn't respond and heads back. He will have his turn with the ball. Wait for that contest!
Stars tries to go full but fails to keep it in line of the stumps. Slips down the leg side and Ishant fails to flick it off his pads.
Misjudges there. He drives a full ball past the gully fielder and wants the second run. But the third man quickly gets around it and only a single is possible. Ishant is exposed to Starc again.
Edgy! Full and outside off, angling across the batsman, Pujara tries to drive it through covers but gets a big fat outside edge down to third man. Denies the single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Width on offer outside off, Pujara cracks it off his back foot through covers for a run.
Full and around off, Pujara flicks it with soft hands through mid-wicket and straightaway shouts two. Completes it with ease.
Too wide outside off, another easy leave for Che.
Serves it on a length outside off, Pujara allows it through to the keeper.
Good length ball around off, angling in and straightening a bit. Right on the button. Pujara defends it off his front foot.
Josh Hazlewood to share the new cherry from the other end.
Comes back to his first ball. Down the leg side, Sharma leaves it alone.
Swing again but this was going down leg. Starc dishes one fuller ball down leg, Sharma misses his flick and gets hit on his leg. Going down leg that.

NOT OUT! Height! Ishant survives. After bowling three down the leg side, Starc bowls one full in line of the stumps. Sharma leaves it alone and the ball comes back in to hit his pads. After an appeal, the umpire raises his finger. Ishant takes the review and the replays show us that it would have gone above the stumps. Good review.
Review! Ishant has left one and the ball comes back in to hit his leg. The umpire thinks it's out. Looks out too. Let's find out in the replays...
3 in a row! Is this some trap? Goes short this time down the leg side, Sharma does not feather it to Paine.
Down leg again. Starc not getting his line right. Sharma lets it be.
Errs down the leg side, Sharma covers his stumps and leaves it alone.
Second new ball has been taken immediately by Australia. Mitchell Starc is back on to make first use of the nut.
Flighted on middle, flicked across the line but straight to short leg.
Shortish and on off, Pujara jumps behind inside the crease and punches it to covers.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it back to the bowler.
Gets on the front foot and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Steps down the track to a full ball and drives it to mid off.
Flatter and on middle, punched back to the bowler.
Bowling change. Travis Head to bowl the final over before the second new ball will be due.
Tossed up ball on middle, nudged in front of square leg for a run. Perfect over for India. Three times they got a couple of runs and a single off the final ball to keep Pujara on strike.
Loopy off spinner on middle, Pujara plays it off his pads towards leg gully.
A touch short and around off, Pujara allows it to spin back in and deflects it through backward point for a couple. Doing it nicely, Che.

Physio is out. Cheteshwar Pujara seems to have pulled his hamstrings while turning for the second run. Hopefully, he is fine. He has batted for 208 balls in this tough hot conditions. Brave batting, showing a lot of character.
Once again Pujara uses his feet and flicks it with the turn to deep square leg. Another couple of runs added to the total.
Full around off, drifting back in, Pujara inside edges his attempted flick past the left side of Finch at leg slip. Two added to the total. 200 up for India!
Walks down the track and then wears it on his pads. It lobs up to short leg.
Bouncer around off, Ishant leans back, drops his wrists and sways away from the line.
Finds the gap at extra cover. A nice looking drive from Pujara, he sends this wide of mid off and takes three. Ishant to face the last delivery.
Back of a length delivery around off, Pujara plays it late and guides it down to deep point. Another run denied.
Another delivery in the channel outside off, Che has nothing to do with it.
Outside off, left alone.
Fullish and outside off, Pujara drives it to the deep cover-point region but turns down the single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Too full and on middle, Ishant goes hard at it and hits it towards mid on.
Shout for an lbw, turned down. Sharma lunges to defend but fails to put bat on ball. Lyon is interested but the impact is outside off.
Works the delivery outside off to the leg side, finds square leg.

FOUR! That's a fine sweep shot from India's number 9. He goes down on one knee to a full ball and uses his long reach to his advantage. Connects well and sends it whistling to the square leg boundary.
Fuller and off, flicked with the spin to short mid-wicket.
Good length ball on off, Che defends it off his back foot to the off side. Over to Ishant now.
A bouncer down the leg side, Pujara allows it through. He will like to bowl one more dot ball so that Lyon has six balls to bowl at Ishant.
Another straight drive by Pujara but this one is not properly timed. He denies the run on offer. That one probably stuck on the surface before reaching the batsman.
Excellent shot! Fuller in length on off, Pujara brings down a straight bat and drives it down the ground to long. A couple taken. This is now his highest Test score in Australia.
Back of a length delivery around off, Pujara goes back and taps it down in the gap at point. Turns down the single.
On a driving length outside off, Pujara takes his front foot forward and then makes a leave.

Not out! Australia lose a review! Down the leg side. Ishant looks to turn that away but misses. It goes off something to Paine at the back. He appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Tim takes it up but replays show us that it came off Sharma's thigh pad.
Review! For caught behind. Paine thinks Ishant has nicked one behind.
Peach! Through the gate. Ishant looks to block this but the back leg of Sharma has saved him. Kisses his pads and goes to the keeper.
Loopy ball on leg, Sharma is struck on his thigh pad.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Played to the mid-wicket region by Pujara. They pick up a single.

Loopy ball on off, Che prods forward to block it but gets hit on his leg. Australia appeal but the umpire stays put. The hosts do not take the review. Good decision as that would have gone to miss the leg pole.
Ishant Sharma is the new man in.

OUT! The 62-run stand has been broken by a jaffa of a delivery. Cummins roars in delight. He dishes in a length delivery on middle and gets it to straighten off the seam after landing. Ashwin's intention is to play on the leg side but he doesn't close the face of the bat in time. It takes the outside half of his blade and flies straight into the hands of Handscomb at second slip. End of a hard-fought knock by Ravichandran Ashwin. India now need their tail to wag. Still 11 short of the 200-run mark.
FOUR! Shot! Lovely hands of Ashwin on display. A length delivery outside off, there is room on offer and Ashwin steers it through point for his first boundary. He has been very patient.
Fullish on off, stroked off the front foot to mid off.
Ashwin has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, cut behind point for a run.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler.

Drinks break. Finally, a wicket-less hour for India as Ashwin and Pujara are amidst a superb partnership. Both batsmen offered a chance each but the Aussie fielders failed to grab those chances. Now, this stand is growing in confidence and the hosts would be hoping to strike back as soon as possilbe.
This one is full and outside off, a nicely floated one, Ashwin strides forward and drives it back.
Another delivery turning back in from a shorter length on off, Ashwin blocks it from the crease.
Flatter and quicker on off, defended off the back foot.

Bat-pad but not carrying to short leg! Slower through the air, full and around off, turning back in, Ashwin tries to defend off the front foot but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It pops out but dies in front of Handscomb.
Extra flight this time, it's full and around off, Ashwin drives it off his front foot to covers.
Tossed up ball on middle, turning back in, Ashwin plays it from the crease past short leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Straying down the leg side, Ashwin picks it off his pads and flicks it through square leg for a run.
Fuller length ball on off, shaping back in a touch, Ashwin offers a straight bat in defense.
Fullish and on off, solidly defended.
Provides width outside off, Ashwin stays back and opens the face of his bat at the last moment. Middles his shot well but finds the gully fielder.
Lands it on a good length around off, Ashwin thrusts forward and blocks it near his front pad.
Pat Cummins is back on.

Spin and bounce back into the batsman from outside off, Che tries to defend but misses. It balloons in the air off his pads, the Aussies get excited but the ball drops safely on the off side. No wood.
Pujara dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball and flicks it with the spin. Doesn't find the gap as it goes straight to the fielder standing near square leg.

Good piece of running between Pujara and Ashwin. They are not known for this. Quicker one down the leg side, Ashwin tries flicking but probably gets a faint inside edge. It goes past leg gully and they take three.
Flicks it with the spin on the leg side but finds the fielder in front of square leg.
Tossed up ball outside off, turning back in from a shorter length outside off, Ashwin is on the back foot as he taps it on the off side.
This one is angled in and is a little too straight. Pujara flicks it through square leg for a couple of runs.

Too full and around off, Pujara forces it out back to the bowler who stops it on one bounce. Tries to show aggression by throwing it at the batsman but he fails to collect the ball cleanly. Josh then stares Pujara. No words hurled.
Goes wide of the crease and spears in a full ball on middle, Pujara keeps it out to mid on.
This one is way wide outside off, Che has nothing to do with it.
Good length delivery on off, Pujara defends it safely off the front foot.
Digs in a short delivery outside off, Pujara leaves it alone.
Strides forward to a full ball and offers a straight bat in defense.
Goes back and hits it across the line. A touch uppish but is safe in front of short leg.

A little shimmy down the track by Pujara as he caresses his on drive. The mid on fielder makes a half stop probably as the ball slows down before the fence. They take three runs and bring up the first 50-run stand for India. A crucial partnership, this.
An off spinner landing around off and turning down the leg side, Che clips it off his pads through square leg for a couple.
Flatter and a touch shorter outside off, Pujara is on the back foot in defense.
Spinning down the leg side, Ashwin moves inside the crease and uses his wrists to flick it behind square leg for a run.
Change of ends for Nathan Lyon.
As soon as Ashwin finds the line to be straighter and the length to be fuller, he takes his front foot forward and flicks it behind square leg for a run.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Ashwin pushes his weight on the back foot and presents a straight bat in defense.
The length is fuller this time, outside off, Ashwin pushes it off his front foot to covers.
Lands it on a length outside off and it holds its line after landing. Ashwin makes an easy leave.
Angles in a good length ball on off, Ashwin presses forward and plays it across the line in the direction of mid on.
Leading edge but safe! A back of a length delivery around off, Ashwin stays back to turn it around but gets a soft leading edge. It goes safely to covers.
Change in bowling from this end. Josh Hazlewood is back on.
Good length ball angling into the batsman, Pujara works it off his pads through mid-wicket and returns for the second run.
Bumper this time, around off, Che ducks underneath it.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, Pujara shoulders arms.
Hurls a length delivery in the channel outside off, Pujara allows it through to the keeper.

The ease with which Ash bats is simply outstanding. Has a sound technique really. Short delivery this time on off, Ashwin is nicely on top of the bounce as he plays it in front of square leg for a run.
Full around off, angling back in, Pujara presents a straight bat and pushes it past the bowler. The mid on fielder moves across to his left to stop the ball and they cross for a run.
And again. Another off spinner has been defended solidly off the front foot by Ashwin.
Floated and on off, spinning back in, Ashwin gets forward and defends it near his front pad.
Lunges to a full ball and flicks it with the spin, finds mid-wicket.
Tossed up ball on middle, defended off the back foot to the leg side.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Off spinner on middle, turned off the pads past short leg for a run.
Length ball on middle and leg, Che turns his bat to the on side.
Full and on the fourth stump line, carved away through cover-point to get his partner on strike.
Back of a length ball around off, Ashwin stays inside and punches it to mid off.
Length ball outside off, Ashwin shoulders his arms to this.
Full and on off, driven past covers for a brace.
Yorker just outside off, Ashwin tries putting bat to ball but doesn't it close to the ball.
Pat Cummins is into the attack.
On the leg side, Pujara uses his feet but flicks it straight to square leg.
Outside off, cut past point for a single.
Full on middle, Ashwin gets to the pitch of it and blocks it.
Covers his stumps and blocks this one out.
On off, kept out by Ashwin.
On the leg side, turned away to square leg.
Length all around off, Che shoulders arms to let that one through.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Fuller ball outside off, Pujara who has been there for 168 balls goes for one outside the off stump. He gets a fat edge which flies just over Khawaja at gully for a boundary. The replays show that Usman got fingertips to this and the ball trickles down to the third man fence. Will go down as a dropped catch but it was Khawaja's brilliance to get something on the ball. He has already taken a blinder in this innings.
Short ball on middle and leg, Ashwin goes for the pull. It goes towards deep square leg for one.
Back of a length all around off, Ashwin gets under it and taps it to the on side.
Fuller in length comes into Ashwin who blocks it out.
Good length ball around off, tapped to the off side.

Shout for an lbw, not given. Flighted on off, turning in, Pujara tries defending but misses. He is hit on the pads, they appeal but impact is outside off. Paine thinks of reviewing it but Lyon tells him that he was playing the shot and also the impact is outside the line.
Flatter and shorter on middle, Ashwin sticks back and hits it across the line past short leg. A single.
Loopy and turning in front around off, Ashwin steps down and tries to defend. It takes a little bit of leading edge before rolling to covers.
Full and flighted on off, flicked behind square leg for a run.
Tossed up ball on middle, tucked on the leg side.
Floated off spinner landing outside off and turning back in, Pujara walks forward and then tries to defend. It takes his pads and goes to the off side. The bowler appeals but nothing from the umpire.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

An overpitched delivery on middle, Pujara gets forward to work it off his pads towards wide mid on. The mid-wicket fielder gets around it but lets it through for the fielder to his left. One run added to the total.
Fractionally short and around off, Pujara covers the line and defends it off his back foot.
Pujara offers the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Play and a miss! A rare lapse in concentration for Pujara! Starc angles across a shortish delivery outside off, Pujara rocks back to slap it through the line but fails to connect. Some extra bounce there to beat the blade.
Short in length and on middle, Ashwin goes on the back foot and helps it down in front of square leg.
Off spinner on middle, Pujara tickles it around the corner, straight to backward square leg.
Uses his wrists again and this time flicks it with the spin past backward square leg. A couple added to the total.
Flatter and fuller on middle, worked with the spin to square leg.
Spin and bounce into the batsman from outside off, Pujara walks down the track and fails to put bat on ball. It goes off his pads to mid-wicket.
Lyon drags his length short and bowls it around off, Pujara rocks back and allows it to spin back in before punching it through point for a couple.
Loopy full ball around off, Pujara walks down the track and kicks it out off his pads.
A touch short and around middle and leg, Ashwin is on his toes in defense.
A good length delivery outside off, going away with the angle, Ashwin shoulders arms.

Fifty for Cheteshwar Pujara, his 20th in this format! A knock of grit and determination. Another delivery on his pads and he works it away to deep square leg for a single. Fine innings by India's reliable number 3. He now needs to continue and add valuable runs with the lower half.
On the pads and eased away through square leg for a couple of runs.
Angling away from the batsman, on a good length, Che allows it through.
Shortish around off, defended off the back foot.
Goes on the back foot to a shortish delivery and blocks it safely.

Dropped? Looks like it. Turn and bounce down the leg side. Ashwin tries working it away but fails to middle his shot properly. It goes off the inside edge to Finch at leg slip who stretches his right hand out but fails to grab it.
Helps it with the spin past short leg for a run.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Yes, the dive has saved Pujara! It all started with a flighted ball on middle. It turned back in a bit as Ashwin tried to defend it off his front foot. But it took the inside edge and went past the right side of the short leg fielder. The leg slip fielder, Aaron Finch, chased it down and threw it to the keeper who broke the stumps. They appealed and the square leg umpire went upstairs. The replays showed that Pujara was safely in. Direct hit was needed.
Appeal for a run out. It's referred upstairs. Is Pujara safe with his dive?
Tossed up ball landing outside off and spinning back in, Ashwin stays back and defends it with an angled bat.
Bouncer down the leg side, Pujara ducks underneath it at the last second. Maiden.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The line is straight again, Che goes on his back foot and turns it on the leg side.
Keeps his line around off and probes with a length delivery, Che covers his stumps and offers a straight bat in defense.
On a good length this time, Pujara works it off his pads but finds the fielder.
Shortish delivery to begin the session. It's outside off and Pujara cracks it off his back foot. Finds point.

We're back for the last session. The men concerned are also back on the field. 34 overs left in the day's play. Mitchell Starc to kick off proceedings. Two slips in place and then there is one fielder standing a few steps ahead of the third slip position.
... Day 1, Session 3 ...

India have limped their way into the Tea break. They lost two wickets in this session as once again their batsmen were quite ordinary with the shot selection. Nathan Lyon was the best bowler on show in the afternoon. He picked up both the wickets and was bowling in good areas. Cheteshwar Pujara is fighting a lone battle but is running out of partners. Currently, Australia are in the driver's seat and they will look to wrap up the innings as quickly as possible. For India, they will be relying on the current partnership to bail them out. Who will succeed? Join us for the last session of the day to find out.
Quicker this time, a touch short and down the leg side, Ashwin tries flicking but misses. That will be Tea on Day 1!
Allows the ball to spin back in and then works it on the leg side by going deep inside the crease.
This time the length is full and Pujara drives it through covers for three runs.
Flatter and shorter on off, Che is on the back foot in defense.
Once again Pujara is down the track to a full ball and helps it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up ball on off, Pujara gets down the track and flicks it with the spin to mid-wicket.
On off, Ashwin comes ahead but decides to block it.
Full on middle and leg, bunted down by Ashwin.
Full and on leg, turned away through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and on off, Ashwin can't get it past mid off.
Overpitched from Head. Ashwin drives it to extra covers for a single.
Full on off, kept out safely off the front foot.
Travis Head called to roll his arm.
Played to the mid-wicket region by Pujara.
Down the leg side, flicked away through square leg to change strike.
Ashwin defends it from within the crease.
Flighted ball on middle, Ashwin blocks it out.
On the leg stump, Ashwin taps it in front of himself.
Off spinner outside off, guided towards short third man.
Fuller in length outside off, driven towards covers.
Around off, punched to the cover region.
Outside off, defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Rare loose delivery from Hazlewood. Short ball outside off, Che cuts it and gets it up and over backward point. No fielder there and he gets four to his name.
Similar line and length, turned away to fine leg for one.
On the pads, flicked away to deep square leg to change ends.
RA has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
In line of the stumps, Ashwin defends it back to the bowler.
Comes down the track and works this through square leg for one.
A bit on the shorter end, pushed to cover-point.
Full and outside off, Pujara dances down and milks it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, Ashwin opens the bat face and guides it towards third man for a run.
Short ball on the leg side, Pujara ducks to evade it.
Fuller in length, Pujara lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and on off, Pujara keeps it out with a full face of the bat.
CP has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Interesting. There is a slip fielder with helmet. He is in a very unfamiliar position. Just to the right of the second slip fielder and very close to the bat.
Fuller ball in line of the stumps, Che blocks it out with a straight bat.
Length ball on leg, Ashwin turns it away to square leg.
Loopy ball outside off, bunted down by Ashwin.
Another slider down leg, flicked away to change strike.
Down leg, Ashwin works it away fine to get off the mark.
On off, Ashwin blocks it out.
On off, Ashwin gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Ravichandran Ashwin is the new man in.

OUT! A long delay but the finger is eventually raised. Lyon has been bowling great and gets another reward to his name. Flighted ball around off. The ball curls away just enough. Pant strides forward to play the trajectory but gets a feather behind due to the away spin. Paine takes the catch and appeals. The umpire stays put but then raises his finger. Pant walks. He was playing all types of aggressive shots but eventually gets out while defending. India in big trouble now.
Bouncer! Pujara gets low and lets the ball through.
Outside off, left alone.
Che has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Edged but just short. Hazlewood has been in that corridor of uncertainty every time. Serves another one there around off, Pujara pushes it with soft hands. It bounces just before the slip cordon and goes through it for a brace.
Outside off, cut to point.
Length ball outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Josh Hazlewood in for another burst.
Outside off, once again nudged to the point region away from his body.
RP has played it to the point region.
Flighted ball on off, driven to covers.
Uses his feet and hits it to long on for another run.
Full on leg, turned away towards mid-wicket to rotate strike.
On middle and leg, tucked away off the back foot towards square leg for one. Playing Lyon off the back foot is the key, not to the shorter ones though.
Length ball around off, kept out by Pant.
Bouncer! Pant gets away from it and leaves it alone.
FOUR! Nice! Elegant! Low full toss around off, Pant drives it in the gap through the cover region. The ball rolls away to the fence. Good batting.
Full and closer to the off stump, Pant from within his crease defends it.
Drags his length a tad back on off, Pant defends it off his back foot.
Full on off, Pant covers his stumps and blocks it out.
Cries of catch it but it's nowhere close to the fielder. On the pads, Pujara flicks it away uppishly towards square leg. Dot ball to complete the over.
Pant works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Looped up on off, bunted down towards silly point.
On off, hit to the off side.
On middle and leg, whipped away through mid-wicket. They manage to come back for the second.
Appeal for an lbw! Inside edge! Loopy ball on middle and off, skidding off the surface, Pant looks to block it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Had he missed that, he was a goner.
Dishes out another bouncer on middle and leg, Che crouches under it.
Back of a length ball on that fourth stump line, Pant taps it with soft hands towards mid off and gets to the other end.
Length ball outside off, Pant points his bat skywards and leaves it alone.
On a good length around off, Pant gets behind it and taps it in front of him.
Pitches this further up on middle, Pant plays it back towards the bowler.
Goes short outside off, Pant ducks under it.
Once again steps out and clips it with the turn to deep mid-wicket. Another brace.
Once again steps out and clips it with the turn to deep mid-wicket. Another brace.
Flatter on off, defended off the back foot.
Uses his feet and flicks it with the spin through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Pujara has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up ball around middle, Pujara comes down the track but then is hit on the pads as he fails to meet the ball.
No! Not really! What a guy! Good length ball outside off. Pant looks to slog this over mid-wicket. Cannot put bat to ball and the ball goes through to the keeper. Ugly.
Pays respect again. Outside off, Pant is happy to defend it. Perhaps got some words from Che?
Fuller ball again around off, Pant bunts it out. Some patience shown by the southpaw.
Full and on middle, Pant blocks it with a straight bat.
Fuller ball outside off, Pant drives it to the off side.
Back of a length ball outside off, Che cuts it close to his body through point for just a run.
Pujara flicks it away with a wristy shot towards backward square leg. They pick up a single.
Gets behind this ball and keeps it out.
CP works it down the leg side.
Long appeal but only from Lyon. Loopy ball around off, Che looks to bunt it but gets hit on his pads outside off. Lyon appeals but the impact was not in line.
Outside off, Pujara cuts it late through backward point for a couple of runs.
Off spinner on middle and leg, Che tucks it away to the on side.

Drinks! Two very different batsmen in the middle. One who only looks to attack while the other is happy to play by the merit. Either way they need to see off this session or else the hosts will not be far away from batting very soon.
Length ball outside off, Pant feels for it but cannot get bat to ball.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh-pad as he fails to flick. Beaten for pace.
Leading edge again. Fuller ball around off. Once again Pant looks to go on the on side but gets a leading edge through to covers. Two more runs collected. Living very dangerously.

FOUR! Edge but safe! That's the way he plays. Attack, attack and attack. Full and outside off, Pant looks to flick it away but gets a leading edge wide of the slip cordon. The ball rolls towards third man for a boundary. Rishabh smiles.

SIX! Lovely! Just the flick of the wrists and it has gone the distance. Full and on the legs, Pant leans forward and rotates his wrists. Makes proper connection and sends it flying over backward square leg for a biggie. 100 up for India.
Not afraid to go for the big ones is Pant. Angled into the pads of Pant who lofts it over mid on for a brace.
Flighted ball on off, Pujara comes forward and pads it out. The ball balloons towards Lyon who takes the catch but there was no bat.
FOUR! The odd ball that is short and Che makes full use of it. Goes on his back foot and punches the ball square of the point fielder for a boundary.
Around off, kept out.
Floated ball on middle and leg, Che comes forward and turns it away with the spin.
Similar ball given air. Pujara uses his feet and pads it out.
Off spinner on off, Pujara taps it in front of himself.
Even better. Perfect from Starc. Bowls fire at 150.8 kph. Nips back in from around off. Pant gets across to play at it but is beaten again.
Length ball outside off. Pant is forward to play at it but the ball just passes the outside edge.
On the legs of Pant who tucks it away to the short mid-wicket fielder.
Misses his line this time. Errs it full but down leg. Pant tries to flick it but misses.
Similar line and length on the pads, this time Pant plays it to square leg.
On a good length on the pads, Pant flicks it away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Uses his feet but is beaten in flight. Tries defending but misses and is hit on the pads.
Turning back in from around off, Pujara moves back to play it with the spin but finds backward square leg.
Slower through the air, full and turning back in, Pujara shimmies down a little and then tries to defend it with his bat and pad together.
Rishabh Pant is the new batsman out in the middle.

OUT! Oh dear! What was Rohit thinking? Brain fade! Really. He played a similar shot on the previous ball and just managed to get it over the ropes but this time falls right into the trap. A bit flat this time from Lyon, on middle and off, Rohit thought it was going to be fuller, but it wasn't. Still goes for the swipe across the line. Gets a top edge on it and the ball flies towards square leg. Harris runs in and takes a simple catch. India have half their side back in the hut and after offering some resistance, Rohit walks back. He will be very disappointed.

SIX! Not the most convincing of ways but another maximum to Rohit's name. Loopy ball on middle, Rohit gets low and sweeps it aerially towards square leg. He gets just enough bat on it. Harris on the square leg rope takes the catch but then just steps outside the boundary line. He throws the ball back in play but was too late in doing so. The umpires check it up and then a biggie is signalled.
Of spinner around off, Rohit plays it on the bounce to the short leg fielder.
Good length ball outside off, Che lets it go.
Back of a length ball on the hips of Rohit who tucks it around the corner for a single.
Full again outside off, Sharma checks his shot as he just pushes it towards short mid off.
Lovely bowling. Gets this one to come in and almost yorks Rohit. Rohit does well and angles the ball away towards the gully region.
A bit fuller on the off pole. Rohit gets behind it and taps it on the off side.
On a good length angled away from Rohit. Good bounce on it as Rohit points his bat skywards and leaves it alone.
Quicker and fuller, Pujara comes down the track to play at it but misses to get hit on the pads.
Spinning down the leg side, Pujara moves back and works it down to fine leg for a brace.
Nearly a catch to short leg! Pujara uses his feet and tries to flick. Fails to control the shot well and it goes just wide of Handscomb.
Turn and bounce from a fuller length around off, Pujara prods to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It dies down quickly in front of short leg.
Another off spinner around off, a bit on the shorter side, Pujara goes back and defends it towards the bowler.
Allows the ball to spin back in and flicks it off his pads to backward square leg.
Nathan Lyon's turn to roll his arm. A slip and short leg for him.
Down the leg side, Pujara nudges it behind square leg and collects a single to retain strike.
Tries to tempt the batsman with another short and wide delivery, initially Pujara looks to play at it but then leaves it alone.
Back of a length delivery on off, Pujara stands back to play inside the line and pushes it to point.
Fullish on off, defended off the front foot to mid off.
Gets carried away this time and miscues his shot. Starc goes full and lands it around off, Pujara tries to blast it through covers but it takes the inside edge and rolls to short mid-wicket.

FOUR! Pujara finally wakes up. He has been defending everything coming his way. Spots the shorter delivery wide outside off, senses the opportunity to free his arms and smashes it over the slip cordon.
Mitchell Starc returns in the attack.
A front foot defense by Rohit to complete the over.
A length ball angling in on off, defended off the back foot.
Sharma has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

SIX! What a shot! This one comes out of nowhere! All timing, no power. Rohit has just caressed his cover drive all the way over the fence. He is a special batsman. Unstoppable in the limited overs and trying to find his feet in Tests as well. Lazy elegance.
Good length ball angling in from around off, Rohit presses forward and defends it from the inner half of his bat to mid on.
Back of a length delivery on off, Pujara immediately goes on the back foot and punches it in the gap at covers for one.
On a driving length outside off, holding its line, Sharma offers no shot. Slow going for India, understandably. They want to build a partnership here.
Angling in on a length around off, Rohit defends it off his back foot.

Goes wide of the crease and spears in a fuller length ball on middle, Rohit leans forward and across to flick but fails to middle it properly. Still it speeds away in the gap at mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Extra bounce around off, Rohit tries defending but gets it off the inside half of the bat.
Puts it on a fuller length around off, Sharma defends it by getting forward.
Short and down the leg side, Rohit tries to pull it across the line but misses.
A rising delivery, cutting back into the batsman from a shortish length outside off, Pujara goes on the back foot and plays it down in front of short leg.
This one is on a length and outside off, Che pushes it gently with an angled bat to the off side.
Sharp delivery, fuller and on off, Pujara dead bats it back to the bowler.
On a good length this time, it's around off and shaping in, Pujara presents a straight bat in defense.
Shortish and around off, Pujara sticks on his crease and taps it down on the off side.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Pujara packs a punch from the back foot but it goes straight to the point fielder.
Outswinger this time, Hazlewood dishing out all his variations. Rohit spots it and allows it through.
Lands it on a good length outside off and gets it to shape back in off the seam. Rohit takes his front leg forward to cover the line and then makes a leave.
Rohit has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bouncer this time, Sharma allows it through.
Goes fuller this time, delivers it on middle, Sharma keeps it out safely in the direction of mid on.
Shortish and on off, Rohit stays back footed and plays it down with an angled bat to backward point.
Good length ball on off, solidly defended from the crease by Pujara.
Bouncer around leg, Pujara allows it through to the keeper.
Short delivery on off, Rohit gets on top of the bounce and pulls it to deep square leg for a run.
Angling into the batsman, Rohit plays it off his front foot towards backward point.
Back of a length ball on off, straightening a bit with extra bounce, Sharma stands open in his stance as he defends it down on the surface.
Fuller and outside off, driven confidently off the front foot but straight towards mid off.
Good length ball on off, Pujara pushes it from the back foot to point. End of the over.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A length delivery on off, Che stays on the back foot in defense. Pushes it out to covers.
Goes full this time and lands it on middle. Rohit tries defending with a straight willow but it takes the inside edge and rolls behind square leg for a single.
Another delivery in the channel outside off, it's left alone by Rohit.
Starts with a good length delivery in the channel outside off, Sharma allows it through.
Josh Hazlewood to bowl from the other end.
Shortish and pulled behind square leg for a run.
A length ball angling back in from around off, Rohit offers a straight bat in defense.
Play and a miss! Good length delivery outside off, going straight on after landing, Sharma pushes inside the line and misses.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Overpitched and duly punished. This is how Rohit Sharma bats. He will always punish the bad balls. It's full and outside off, Rohit leans forward and caresses it through covers.
Right on the button. Full and angling in around off, Rohit gets forward and defends it with a straight bat.

We are back after Lunch. If you're in India, then breakfast. Whatever, as long as you are not hungry. The players have made their way out. Cheteshwar Pujara and Rohit Sharma walk out to take center stage.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The surface offered good assistance to the seamers early on and credit should be given to the Aussie speedsters for hitting accurate lines and lengths. They kept asking difficult questions to the batsmen and succeeded in creating good pressure. Nathan Lyon has also got good purchase from the pitch as he kept it tidy and was unlucky not to get the wicket of Rahane when he was on 2. Plenty of work needed to be done by the Indian middle-lower order. Do join us in a short while for more action.

Excellent morning session for Australia! They lost the toss but then their pacers provided them with the best start possible. Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood got into the act immediately and removed the Indian openers cheaply. Pat Cummins hunted down the big fish, Virat Kohli and then after offering a brief resistance, Ajinkya Rahane was dismissed. It's been a very indisciplined batting effort by India. All the four wickets went down due to loose shots attempted and they will be deeply disappointed at the moment.
Hurls in a length delivery outside off, Pujara has nothing to do with it. That will be Lunch on Day 1!
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump. Showing good patience, Che.
Make it four leaves but this one is a shorter one around off. Che drops his wrists, leans back and then allows it to the keeper.
Third ball in a row lands in the same region. Pujara is also repeating his treatment. Left alone.
Angling across the batsman, on a length outside off, Pujara takes a stride forward and then allows it through.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Sharma has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Square leg drops back.
Soft outside edge. Back of a length delivery on off, Rohit stays back to play inside the line and does well to do so with gentle hands. The outside edge doesn't carry to the slip cordon.

SIX! It has gone all the way! Sharma loves playing pull shots and this one is a shot of authority. Cummins digs it in, on middle and sits up nicely for the batsman. Rohit rides the bounce and pulls it in front of square leg for a biggie. Pat smiles and shares a few words with Sharma. It has begun.
This time Sharma is nicely forward to a full ball and pushes it out on the off side.
An absolute beauty to beat Sharma all ends up. Late away movement there after it lands on a length around off. Rohit without any footwork tries playing at it and gets beaten.
Rohit has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pat Cummins is brought back into the attack. A little over 5 minutes to go for Lunch.
Full and on off, Pujara dead bats it.
Bouncer this time, Pujara safely ducks under it.
Digs in a short ball around leg, Rohit moves inside the line of the delivery and helps his pull shot down to fine leg for a run. Didn't look entirely in control. 50 up for India!
Angling across the batsman, wide outside off, Rohit makes yet another leave.
This one is closer to the off stump line and on a fuller length. Rohit covers his stumps and then shoulders arms.
Starts with a shortish delivery in the zone outside off, Sharma allows it through.
Tim Paine is rotating his fast bowlers well here. He brings in Mitchell Starc after a short spell by Josh Hazlewood.
Advances down the track to a full ball and brings his bat and pad together in defense.
A back foot punch this time, towards extra cover and a single is picked.
FOUR! Loopy off spinner outside off, Rohit takes his front leg forward and drives it crisply on the up through covers. Finds the gap and fetches his first boundary.
Too full and outside off, driven off the front foot but straight to the cover fielder.
A touch flatter and shorter outside off, Sharma plays it late by opening the face of his bat. He runs it down in the direction of third man and takes a couple.
Flighted and outside off, turning back in, Rohit goes back and punches it to covers.
Shortish and on middle, played down in front of short leg.
Pitches it up and outside off, Pujara gets forward and defends it back.
Wrong line this time. Back of a length delivery around middle and leg, angling further down, Pujara lifts his bat and moves away from the line of ball.
Hurls a length delivery in the channel outside off, it's left alone watchfully by Pujara.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.

Edged but safe! Full length ball around off, shaping away a bit, Pujara tries defending it with a straight bat but gets a soft outside edge behind. Luckily for him, it doesn't carry to the slip cordon.

In the air... taken! But off the pads. Flighted ball on middle, Rohit looks to turn this away but gets it off his thigh pad. The ball balloons in the air, Handscomb, from short leg takes it but the umpire is not interested.
In line of the stump, Rohit bunts it down.
Loopy ball on middle and leg, Sharma gives it on the bounce to short leg.
On off, Sharma waits for it and taps it out.
Gives this air on middle, Rohit plays it with a straight bat.
Off spinner on leg, tucked away around the corner by Rohit.
In the zone outside off, Pujara has nothing to do with it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Straighter in line, Rohit tucks it through square leg and is off the mark with a single.
A bouncer to greet the new batsman, Rohit ducks underneath it rather uncomfortably.
Rohit Sharma arrives in the middle with India in tatters. Can he transform his shorter version form in Tests?

OUT! Add another one to the tally for Australia. Like his teammates, Rahane has also gone chasing a wide delivery. Hazlewood just lands it on a length and wide outside off. Gets a hint of away movement as well. Rahane could have left it easily but goes after it away from his body. Tries driving without his front foot entirely forward and gets a big outside edge behind. Peter Handscomb makes no mistake (this time) at second slip. Good bowling change by Paine. India's misery continues. Their batsmen seem to be in love with driving but they should be doing that on the roads of India, not here.
Starts this spell with a length ball on middle and leg, going down with the angle, Pujara fails to flick and it goes off his pads to backward square leg. A leg bye taken.
Bowling change. Josh Hazlewood is back to have another go. He was brilliant in his first spell.
Flighted one, full and around off, curling back in, Rahane draws forward and defends it well.
Loopy full ball on off, Rahane lunges and defends it watchfully.
Off spinner on the shorter side outside off, Pujara gets back and punches it square of the wicket on the off side for a run.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it towards short leg.
Flighted off spinner around off, a bit on the shorter side, Pujara gets back and punches it back.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball and bunts it wide of mid off for a brisk single.
Skidding off the surface after landing on a good length around off. Pujara once again defends it from the crease to the on side.
Good length ball on off, Pujara stays back footed in defense.
In the region outside off again, Pujara has nothing to do with it.
This one shoots off the surface. On a length outside off, Pujara shoulders arms.
In a good channel, Pujara chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Rahane has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Uppish but wide of short leg this time! Tossed up ball on middle, an off spinner, Rahane tries working it around but it takes the inside edge onto his pads and flies past the outstretched left hand of short leg. Rahane is living dangerously.
This time Pujara flicks it past short leg for a run.
Works it with the turn to the on side but finds short leg.
Tossed up and outside off, Che plays it down with an angled bat to point.
Loopy and spinning back in, Pujara tries defending but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Another easy leave outside the off stump to end the over.
Tempting line, this. Full and outside off, there to be driven, but Rahane gets forward and allows it through.
Lands it on a length outside off, holding its line, Rahane pushes inside the line with gentle hands and it goes off the outer half of the bat to gully.
A hint of extra bounce there from a length around off, Jinx defends it off his back foot.
On a length and outside off this time, Rahane pushes it off his front foot to covers.
Full and around off, angling in, Pujara leans forward and across before flicking it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run. A bit of an inside edge there.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! This is what they have been trying to do. They don't want Nathan Lyon to settle down and hence using their feet a lot. Once again Rahane shimmies down the track to a full ball and swings it with the spin over mid-wicket. Interestingly, Jinx doesn't hit a lot of sixes in T20 cricket but has done so on the first morning of a Test match. Hmm...
Rahane dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Flighted off spinner outside off, Rahane strides forward in defense.
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball and pushes it off the inside edge to mid on.
Turning back into the batsman from around off, Rahane goes deep inside the crease and defends it towards short leg.
Too full and pacey, at 146.2 kph, Pujara digs it out at the last moment.
Length ball on middle, some extra bounce, Pujara gets back and taps it down to short leg.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. One run added to the total.
On a length outside off, Rahane punches it through extra cover for a couple of runs.
A length ball moving back into the batsman, Rahane pushes it off his pads to mid on.
Full and around off, defended down from the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Allows the ball to spin back in and defends it.

In the air... DROPPED! Rahane gets an early reprieve. Keaton Jennings of late has made these catches look easy for England. Australia have seen Matt Renshaw also doing the same but he ain't playing. Another off spinner, turning back in with extra bounce, Rahane is well forward as he tries to flick but it goes uppishly and quickly towards short leg. Peter Handscomb fails to hold onto the catch and they cross.
Once again Che uses his feet to an off spinning delivery and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Walks froward to flick but fails to middle his shot properly.
Spin and bounce straightaway. Pujara tries defending but misses and is hit high on the pads.
Time for some off spin! Nathan Lyon to roll his arm now.

Drinks! What an hour of play for the Aussies. Couldn't have asked for a better start. 3 wickets which includes the big fish, Virat Kohli. India need to be patient. Too many loose shots have caused their downfall.
Rahane picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Crowd catch! Fuller ball outside off. Rahane puts his bat down and plays at it and it goes straight to point but on the bounce.
Good from Rahane. This one is fuller outside off, Rahane is not bothered to play at it.
Back of a length ball aimed at the hips of Rahane who hops and tucks it onto the ground.
Good leave! On a good length around off, Rahane watches it carefully and shoulders his arms to it.
Length ball around off, Rahane leans ahead and pushes it to covers.
Beauty! On a good length around off, Che comes forward to put bat to it but the ball nips back in and goes between bat and pad through to the keeper.
Goes short outside off again, Pujara ducks to get under it.
FOUR! Shot, nicely played. The pressure is released, momentarily. Back of a length ball outside off, Pujara on his toes punches it behind backward point to earn himself a boundary.
Mixes his length, pitches this one full and outside off, Pujara lets it be.
On a good length, closer to the off pole. Che tries guiding it past gully but cannot get it past him.
A bit on the shorter side outside off, Pujara sways away from it.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
A real gift to Rahane first up. A low full toss, Rahane drives it through covers for a couple of runs.
Ajinkya Rahane is in next.

OUT! Stunner by Khawaja to remove India's best batsman! You need something incredible to dismiss Virat Kohli. Australia are ecstatic, they know the value of this wicket. India in deep trouble. Once again an Indian batsman is caught playing away from the body. Cummins serves this one on a good length and outside off, Kohli goes for a drive and gets a big fat outside towards gully. Now, the real action begins. Khawaja is stationed there. It's to his stronger side. So, he throws himself in the air to his left and takes a one-handed stunner. Superman stuff!
Once again keeps it full and around off, Kohli comes on the front foot again and pushes it to covers.
Full and outside off, Virat draws forward and defends it on the leg side.
First bowling change. It's time to unleash Pat Cummins into the attack.
Quite wide outside off, Pujara is in no mood to chase it away from his body.

Movement off the seam. Once again Josh is asking the question. This one nips back in from a good length outside off, Kohli is forward and hangs his bat out in defense. But it takes the inside edge and squirts behind square leg for a run.
Edgy! Just a hint of late movement. Hazlewood gets this ball around off, Kohli plays inside the line with soft hands and it goes off the outside edge towards gully.
Back of a length delivery on off, Kohli stays back and taps it down to backward point.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, Kohli strides forward to cover the line and shoulders arms.
Digs in a bouncer, Kohli sits underneath it comfortably.
A little short in length around middle, Kohli goes on his toes and nicely works it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Pitches it on a length and outside off, Kohli takes a stride forward and tries to push it through covers. But it comes off the inner half of the bat and rolls in the direction of mid off.
Shortish and outside off, Kohli chooses to leave it.

A crisp drive from Kohli but that will encourage Starc. He got the Indian skipper playing away from the body. Fuller and outside off, at 147.9 kph, Kohli plays the drive square of the field on the off side. Straight to the point fielder.
On a good length this time, Kohli flicks it off his pads to the leg side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
This is the contest we all were waiting for. Starc vs Kohli. It begins with a short delivery around off, angling away, Kohli sways away from the line of fire.
Shortish around off, it's blocked in the direction of wide mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Off the mark is the Indian skipper. Just tucks a shortish delivery on the leg side, finds the gap and runs across to the other end.
Fuller and angling in, Kohli defends it towards mid-wicket.
A firm flick by Pujara which goes behind square leg after hitting the short leg fielder. They cross for a run.
Bowls it outside off, Pujara allows it through.
In walks India's talisman who just loves playing at the Adelaide Oval - Virat Kohli.

OUT! It's edged behind! Murali Vijay is gone. Starc jumps in joy. India have lost both their openers, cheaply. Mitch has been mixing up his length quite nicely. He follows up the previous shorter one by serving a juicy full delivery outside off. Vijay is lured into the drive but the ball doesn't come back in enough. It almost holds its line, takes the outside edge and goes into the gloves of Paine. He was nowhere near to the delivery, his front foot went missing. Vijay is on his way back. Best possible start for Australia after losing the toss.

Ooohhh...a rising delivery. Climbing onto the batsman around off, Vijay does well to fend at it with soft hands. As a result, the outside edge doesn't carry and speeds past the diving gully fielder. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Shortish and wide outside off, Murali shoulders arms.
Action replay of the previous delivery. Another one drifting down the leg side as Starc is unable to control his line. Murali once again fails to get any wood behind it.
Wrong line this time. On a good length and sliding down the leg side, Vijay tries flicking but misses.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Vijay is firmly on the back foot as he blocks it down safely.
Straighter delivery, Vijay tucks it behind square leg and keeps strike with himself.

FOUR! First boundary of this Test match! A loose one though. Vijay is caught playing away from his body. It's full and wide outside off, Murali chases it and slices his drive off the outside half. Luckily for him, it goes aerially but safely through backward point for a boundary.
In the channel outside off, Murali shoulders arms.
Delightful drive. Hazlewood bowls it full and around off, Vijay strokes it through extra cover for a couple of runs. Australia won't mind a batsman driving at this stage with the ball moving around.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Vijay leans back a bit and then makes a leave.
That's a good patient leave. Hazlewood lands it on a length outside off and it holds its line after pitching, Vijay has nothing to do with it.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump. Testing over by Starc!
Bouncer, well-directed, Pujara fends it away off his gloves. Luckily it doesn't carry to the backward short leg fielder who is standing a few steps behind than the usual position.
This one is dug in short and wide outside off, an easy leave this time for Pujara.
Beaten this time! Third delivery in a row is in the off stump channel and going across the batsman with the left-armer's angle. Pujara with no footwork pushes inside the line and misses.
Once again Starc probes around with a length delivery in the outside off channel, Pujara is very watchful as he leaves again.
Puts it on a length outside off, angling away from the batsman, Pujara allows it through.
Movement back into the batsman from around off, Vijay tries to defend but gets an inside edge. It rolls to mid-wicket. End of another good over by Hazlewood.
Identical to the last delivery, once again Vijay is quite solid in his forward defense.
Nicely played! Full and swinging in from outside off, Vijay takes a confident stride forward and defends it to covers.
Tennis ball bounce there. Jumping onto the batsman from a back of a length around off, Vijay is on his toes as he defends it down.
The line is straight from Josh, Pujara rotates his wrists and works it towards short leg. Harris there fails to stop it and it deflects towards mid-wicket. Pujara completes a run.
Angles in a full length ball on middle and leg, Pujara plays it off his pads towards mid on.
Inswinger, pitching full and on middle, Pujara flicks it across the line behind square leg. The fine leg fielder cuts it off and Che is off the mark with a single.
Another delivery in the corridor of uncertainty, leaving the batsman with the angle, Che guards his stumps and makes a leave.
Building good pace, Starc. Slants across a short length delivery outside off, at 145.6 kph, Pujara allows it through.
Lands it on a length outside off, Pujara with an unsure footwork defends it back. His front foot went nowhere.
Lovely delivery and nicely played too. Full and on middle, shaping back in, Vijay works it behind square leg and takes a single.
Beaten! Angling away from the batsman, on a length and leaving the batsman, Vijay has a tentative push inside the line and misses.
Cheteshwar Pujara is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Rahul is caught at third slip! Early blow to India. This is beautiful bowling by Hazlewood. He's getting the ball to move both ways and hunts down one of the Indian openers. Serves it full enough outside off to entice a drive from Rahul. But it's an away swinger which takes a thick outside edge and settles into the big hands of Finch. KL's poor form continues.
Good length delivery angling down the leg side, Rahul tries working it around but misses.
Shaping back into the batsman, Vijay goes at it with soft hands and gets an inside edge. It probably brushes his pads and rolls towards wide mid on. Vijay is off the mark with a single.
This is extraordinary bowling. Last delivery nipping back in, this one left the batsman. It pitches around off and moves away, Vijay pushes inside the line without much footwork and is beaten.

Bat-pad but it's wide of short leg. Nervy start for Murali. This one seams back in from a length around off. Vijay tries to defend it with a straight bat but it takes the inside half of the bat and pops out off his pads.
Nice start from Josh. Bowls it full and angling in around off, Vijay is forward just a bit as he defends.
Josh Hazlewood to share the new ball from the other end.
Zippy delivery, on a length outside off, Rahul strides forward and then lets it go at the last moment. Good beginning, for both teams.
This one is very full, almost lands behind the stump line, Rahul has nothing to do with it.
India are off the mark! Starc spears in a full length delivery on middle at 144.5 kph, Rahul flicks it off his pads through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Great leave! Starc pitches it on a length just outside off and it nips back in a shade. Rahul takes a stride forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
Serves it further up, nice and full outside off, not much swing. Rahul tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
First ball of the series is nice and straight on a good length, KL Rahul gets behind the line and blocks it safely.

Out come the Australian players on the field. Murali Vijay and KL Rahul are the Indian openers. Mitchell Starc has the brand new cherry in his hand. Three slips and a gully in place along with a short leg. It's show time...
The players are out in the centre for the national anthem. We're minutes away from the first ball.

Australia's skipper, Tim Paine says that he would have batted too. Mentions that the boys are excited and are up for the challenge. On his playing XI, he informs that the three fast bowlers and Lyon can do the job for them. On their batting, he replies that they have had good domestic seasons and are in form.

India's skipper, Virat Kohli says that they will bat first. Mentions that the pitch is nice and hard with a nice covering of grass. States that adding runs on the board is always handy. Reckons that this is a difficult challenge to play in Australia. Further says that they are not taking anything for granted and lightly. On him playing in Adelaide, he says that he loves coming here and getting runs. Ends by saying that Rohit Sharma gets the nod as he can play aggressive cricket towards the end and can bat well with the tail.
TOSS - India have won the toss and will bat first.

Pitch report - Brendon Julian is near the playing area giving his thoughts about the surface. Starts by informing that the drop-in pitch has been used in Adelaide for the last 5 years. Adds that there is a good covering of grass and it will seam a little bit at the start but it will be slow on the first day. Mentions that the surface will quicken up as the Test progresses. Advises that as a batsman, if you get through the first hour, sessions 2 and 3, followed by the next two days will be a batting paradise.

The first match of a series is always gripping. Just like a blank canvas with an artist waiting to work on it. You never know what is to come. Hello and welcome to our coverage. It's game time. Australia go in with the extra specialist batsman while for the visitors it's going to be a shootout between Rohit and Vihari. Never before have India come Down Under and been favorites as we mentioned earlier but no game has ever been won on paper. Both teams have a lot to prove and it will certainly take some gritty cricket to come on top. Don't go too far away. Toss coming up shortly...

Oh, this feeling of nostalgia. There's something special about covering or watching a Test match played Down Under. This is the first occasion in my lifetime, India are starting as favourites. They're supposed to win their first-ever Test series in Australia and more than their ranking and recent supremacy in this format, it's because the Aussies are a depleted unit. The Kohli-led team though has tried its best to downplay the situation by calling the Kangaroos a tough nut to crack in their own backyard. Hmm... no one wants to take the pressure of a favourite tag these days, so what it's the number one Test team, so what it's the 'best touring Indian team in last 15 years'... Anyway, enough talk. The Adelaide Oval is ready. Australia are ready. India are ready. Fans are ready. Then what are we waiting for??? Let's dive in. More updates coming your way...
